hints.title: Column-to-Row Inversion
hints.text: Transposing tabular data requires gathering words in the same horizontal column across all lines and outputting them as a single line. How can an associative array buffer words indexed by column?

hints.title: Associative Field Accumulation
hints.text: Iterate through each row record. For field index i from 1 to the number of fields, append the field value to an accumulator array keyed by i, prepending a space if an entry already exists.

hints.title: Buffer Flushing in Final Block
hints.text: Use an awk program with a row loop that builds array entries for each column index. In the completion action block, iterate from 1 to the field count and print each combined column string.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: R: number of rows in file.txt
C: number of columns in file.txt
complexity.notes: Single stream traversal buffering matrix tokens into associative arrays before flushing transposed lines.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Reading the entire file with repeated head and cut invocations in nested loops incurs O(R * C^2) process spawn overhead and fails on larger files.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Buffering transposed tokens in awk memory provides linear single-pass performance at the cost of proportional string memory.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Handling variable numbers of rows and columns cleanly and managing spaces between concatenated tokens without trailing whitespace.

solutions.approach: Field Processing via Associative Array Accumulation in awk
